absent: Full entry prologue of control dispatcher including privilege validation, message framing and sequence handling.
Definitions and initial values of global tree list, hash table, locks, counters and enable state.
Numeric values of operation codes, error codes, terminal bits, lock state and notification flags.
Sizes and numeric values for hash table, cache line width and path maximum.
Complete layouts of tree, chunk, node, mark, watch, rule and signal structures beyond observed members.
Semantics of pathname resolution, path collection and release, containment testing and reference handling.
Semantics of filesystem notification group and mark operations including find, add, detach, reference and free callbacks.
Semantics of audit logging primitives including buffer lifecycle, formatting, untrusted string handling and delivery.
Semantics of security context conversion, LSM property checks and user namespace mapping.
Rule parsing, matching, list numbering and execution mark attachment beyond change and free paths.
Watch creation and parent linkage as well as rule to watch association.
Concurrency ordering with subsystems outside these fragments and interrupt or preemption constraints.

findings.text: The central control routine dispatches configuration messages for adding, deleting and listing rules, trimming trees, establishing path equivalence, reporting signal identity, and querying or updating terminal auditing state. It enforces a locked enable mode that refuses mutation, emits a configuration change record for most outcomes, normalizes success to zero while preserving negative error codes, and handles variable length payloads with explicit size checks.

Rule updates accept only add and delete kinds, translate the opaque payload into an entry object, call the matching add or delete helper, record a rule change outcome, and when the operation fails or represents a deletion release any attached tree reference and execution mark before freeing watch, LSM fields, key and entry memory.

Equivalence handling resolves both the old and new locations, gathers mount coverage for the new location, walks the global tree set with barrier and cursor markers while holding the filter mutex except across blocking resolution, keeps a per tree reference during unlock, checks containment of each watched path beneath the old location, tags covering inodes, then either clears transient marks on full success or trims them on failure.

Trimming walks the global tree set with a cursor and per tree reference, releases the filter mutex while resolving each pathname and collecting ancestor paths, marks chunk owners tentatively then clears the mark where the inode key still matches current paths, prunes stale attachments, and relies on a header no operation variant when the feature is disabled at build time.

String extraction validates that the cursor is present with non zero length inside the remaining budget and within the filesystem maximum, allocates space for payload plus terminator, copies bytes, terminates, and advances the cursor and remaining count for the next field.

Several audit tree and watch helpers exist in two forms sharing one name: a full function that manipulates trees, marks or watches, and a header no operation that either does nothing or reports invalid input. This duality lets callers compile unchanged whether directory watching, trimming, tagging, reference release or mark removal is enabled.

Logging helpers record rule removal with operation label, directory path, key and list number, and record keys with a label followed by either an untrusted string or an explicit null marker. Callers skip logging entirely when auditing is disabled or when buffer allocation fails.

When the global enable state indicates locked, rule addition, rule deletion, trimming and equivalence establishment are refused without changing watched state. Some paths still emit a configuration change record describing the refused operation before returning a permission error.

Unpacked strings must satisfy non null cursor, length greater than zero, length not exceeding remaining bytes, and length not exceeding the filesystem maximum. Violations map to distinct invalid versus too long failures, allocation failure maps to memory shortage, and success always yields a terminated buffer with updated cursor state.

Terminal auditing state consists of two independent boolean flags for enablement and password logging. Queries report both flags from a single atomic read. Updates accept only zero or one for each flag, reject other values as invalid, atomically exchange the stored bitmask, and log old and new values with a success indicator.

The top bit of each owner index serves as a transient tag during trim and equivalence operations. Trim sets the bit for all owners then clears it where the inode key matches a current path. Tagging sets the bit for newly attached owners. Lookup strips the bit before locating the containing chunk, and pruning treats presence of the bit as selection for removal.

Each watched inode maps to a numeric key derived from the address of its notification mark membership. Hash placement divides that key by the cache line width and reduces modulo the table size. Insertion requires a non zero key, issues a one time warning otherwise, and publishes only after full initialization with an ordering barrier.

Tree, watch and chunk lifetimes use reference counting with deferred reclamation. Tree acquisition increments and release decrements with freeing through RCU. Watch release warns if a parent remains or rules remain attached. Chunk allocation starts with a single reference and replacement retires old storage through RCU after publishing the successor.

The filter mutex serializes global tree list traversal, cursor and barrier movement, rule detachment and list membership changes. Holders drop it across blocking pathname resolution while retaining a tree reference, then reacquire and revalidate liveness through the goner indicator before mutating.

A hash spin lock protects chunk membership lists, owner indices and back pointers, root pointers and same root linkage, goner flags, hash linkage and mark to chunk association. It is held for marking, reordering, hash insert, replace and removal, and released across blocking untag work with revalidation on reacquisition.

A filesystem notification group lock stabilizes mark attachment during lookup, creation and teardown, ordered before the hash lock. Hash readers observe chunks through RCU with a write barrier before publication and list replacement primitives. Rule teardown uses RCU deletion with an additional grace wait when execution marks are present, and chunk retirement uses deferred callbacks.

The observed tree object carries a reference count, global list linkage, a list of chunk owners, a list of rules, a pathname, a root chunk pointer, same root linkage and a goner flag. The observed chunk carries hash linkage, a trees list, a live capacity count, a reference count, a numeric key, a mark pointer and a flexible owner array where each element holds list linkage, an index with tag bit and a back pointer.

The observed mark wrapper embeds a notification mark plus a current chunk pointer with bidirectional linkage between mark and chunk. Terminal status carries enable and password flags. Signal replies carry a user identifier, a process identifier and a variable length security context. Rule payloads begin with a fixed header whose size is validated before conversion.

A tree starts active with root and chunk attachments, transitions to goner exactly once when the root disappears and the object is not already retiring, then leaves the global list, detaches rules with logging, prunes remaining chunks and drops its final reference. Removal of an owner clears root linkage when it references the affected chunk.

Chunk evolution either shrinks to nothing, in which case it leaves hash and trees, detaches its mark and schedules deferred freeing, or replaces itself with a newly allocated chunk that inherits the key, adopts surviving owners with compacted indices and refreshed list links, transfers root pointers, swaps the mark association, then publishes through RCU while the predecessor is retired.

Tagging acts as a transaction with a barrier separating preexisting trees from new arrivals. New attachments arrive marked. Full success clears all marks. Any failure trims marked attachments and may retire trees. Rule entries move from parsed to installed on add success, otherwise to freed after releasing tree, mark, watch and LSM resources with outcome logging.

Blocking pathname resolution without the filter mutex risks observing concurrent retirement, mitigated by extra references and goner checks. Dropping the hash lock before untagging risks mark detachment races, mitigated by extra mark references and rechecking attachment state and chunk identity under the group lock. Allocation failures, oversized payloads and missing log buffers are handled as errors or silent skips without partial linkage.

Control vocabulary includes rule addition under AUDIT_ADD_RULE and removal under AUDIT_DEL_RULE with listing under AUDIT_LIST_RULES, maintenance under AUDIT_TRIM and AUDIT_MAKE_EQUIV, identity query under AUDIT_SIGNAL_INFO, terminal handling under AUDIT_TTY_GET plus AUDIT_TTY_SET, and change records under AUDIT_CONFIG_CHANGE.

Failure vocabulary includes invalid input under EINVAL and permission refusal under EPERM with memory shortage under ENOMEM and name too long under ENAMETOOLONG plus no space under ENOSPC, enable lock state under AUDIT_LOCKED, terminal bits under AUDIT_TTY_ENABLE plus AUDIT_TTY_LOG_PASSWD, notification mask under FS_IN_IGNORED with attach flag under FSNOTIFY_MARK_FLAG_ATTACHED, hashing scale under L1_CACHE_BYTES plus HASH_SIZE, allocation mode under GFP_KERNEL and path bound under PATH_MAX.

LSM field selection covers subject user under AUDIT_SUBJ_USER and subject role under AUDIT_SUBJ_ROLE and subject type under AUDIT_SUBJ_TYPE plus sensitivity under AUDIT_SUBJ_SEN with clearance under AUDIT_SUBJ_CLR, and object user under AUDIT_OBJ_USER with role under AUDIT_OBJ_ROLE and type under AUDIT_OBJ_TYPE plus low level under AUDIT_OBJ_LEV_LOW with high level under AUDIT_OBJ_LEV_HIGH.
